verdict.rationale: Ollama is built to run on your own hardware. It has a one-line install script, local base URLs and a REST API for running and managing models, and docs stating that locally run work never leaves the machine. Community users confirm running it themselves on Linux and AMD GPUs, including via ROCm containers. missing for 10: first-party docs on server/container deployment and configuration depth (community notes server configs such as mlock are hidden), plus clarity that Cloud-hosted larger models are not self-hostable.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Nothing you run locally ever leaves your machine.
Ollama has a REST API for running and managing models.
They have shipped ROCm containers since 0.1.27.
Ollama is definitely the easiest way to run LLMs locally
